name: Mexico City
title: Holidays in Mexico City
intro: Pyramids, colourful boats and some of the best food on earth. Here's what Mexico City is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The city is 2,240 metres up, so take the first day gently. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: March, April, October and November are dry and warm. The Day of the Dead at the start of November is colourful and family-friendly. June to September brings short afternoon downpours, but mornings are usually fine. Evenings can be cool all year because the city is so high.

things.name: Teotihuacan
things.blurb: Climb the huge Pyramid of the Sun, about an hour from the city.

things.name: Xochimilco
things.blurb: Float along canals in a brightly painted trajinera boat, with music and snacks.

things.name: Chapultepec Park
things.blurb: A giant park with a castle, a lake, a zoo and lots of museums.

things.name: National Museum of Anthropology
things.blurb: The Aztec Sun Stone and life-size Maya temples.

things.name: Papalote Children's Museum
things.blurb: A big hands-on museum with a planetarium and a dome cinema.

things.name: Frida Kahlo Museum
things.blurb: The bright blue house where the artist lived. Tickets sell out, so book ahead.

faqs.question: Is Mexico City good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's friendly and full of things for children, from pyramids to parks and museums. Stay in a calmer area such as Roma, Condesa or Polanco, and use registered taxis or ride apps.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Five to seven nights covers the city and Teotihuacan. Many families add a beach week on the Caribbean coast or in Oaxaca.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders don't need a visa for a holiday. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: What about the altitude?
faqs.answer: At 2,240 metres, some people get headaches or tire quickly at first. Drink plenty of water and plan an easy first day.
